# apify-bot-guard

> Fair free-plan allowances for Apify Actors (or any free tier), in Python and JavaScript, with no runtime dependencies. At run start `admit()` returns one decision (allowed, remaining, message); the run delivers up to `remaining` and calls `close()`. Limits per user per Actor, per user across Actors, per run, and a pool per Actor, by month, rolling week or day, in results or in cost. Paying users are never limited. Every setting is a `BOT_GUARD_*` env var or a code argument.

Packages: `pip install "apify-bot-guard[apify]"` (Python 3.10+, import `apify_bot_guard`), `npm install apify-bot-guard` (Node 20+, ESM, types included).

## Docs

- [AI integration guide](https://github.com/tacps126/apify-bot-guard/blob/main/docs/AI-INTEGRATION.md): step-by-step for an AI assistant adding the guard to a project, with copy-paste code and checks
- [README](https://github.com/tacps126/apify-bot-guard/blob/main/README.md): overview, decision fields, install, backends, settings summary, cost
- [Configuration reference](https://github.com/tacps126/apify-bot-guard/blob/main/docs/CONFIGURATION.md): every setting, env var name, default, who is limited, identity fields, failure behaviour, recipes
- [Design](https://github.com/tacps126/apify-bot-guard/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md): allowance formula, storage format, writing a backend
